figures.caption: Table 1. The comparative experiments on MRSpineSeg dataset demonstrate the strong semi-supervised spine segmentation capability of our method. The mean Dice and mIoU values are reported and the best results are highlighted in bold.
Fig. 3. Our method shows superior segmentation visualization results on 5% labeled data, compared to SSL and VLM methods.

Fig. 2. Overview of our CPS4. In stage 1, we perform class-specific consistency constrained VLM pretraining to train the vision and text encoder, where token- and pixellevel attention losses are proposed to boost the consistency between class prompts and spine units. Note: In stage 1, we only show the calculation process of {Lumbar Vertebra 1} class, for other classes in the MRI, the calculation process is consistent. In stage 2, we conduct class prompt–driven semi-supervised segmentation to train the segmentation network, where the pseudo label is enhance through class prompt generated segmentation map.
Fig. 1. Our proposed CPS4 generates class prompt guided segmentation map, enhancing the quality of pseudo labels in semi-supervised spine segmentation.

Fig. 4. (a) Ablation study on various components demonstrates the effectiveness of each component in CPS4. (b) Ablation on different ratio of data labeled shows that CPS4 has better data robustness with a subtle decrease when the labeled training data reduce to 5%.

Fig. 5. Visualization of class-specific attention maps. The first row shows ground-truth annotations, the second row presents attention maps produced by our method, and the third row shows results from MedCLIP. Our method exhibits stronger consistency between class prompts and spine units, with attention highly aligned to each corresponding spine units.
